sources.title: CIA, Rhodesia: The Parties to the Dispute
sources.finding: Reports ZIPRA cadres receiving both guerrilla and conventional training, including overseas training, while rapid expansion also includes trainees. Reports ZANLA training and discipline weaknesses. This is a contemporary intelligence judgement, not an impartial census or a rating for every fighter.

sources.title: Department of State, Projected Course of the Mozambique Rebellion
sources.finding: Distinguishes trained officer-potential cadres from recruits receiving short training; highlights shortages of trained leadership and offensive capability. Contains Portuguese claims that should not be treated as objective descriptions of every FRELIMO fighter.

sources.title: CIA Mozambique national intelligence survey retrospective
sources.access: Official indexed primary text; direct PDF redirected to CIA homepage in this run
sources.finding: Describes initial overseas training, subsequent cadre training and small-unit operations; supports development beyond the initial 1965 snapshot, but does not establish an exact month when every unit improved.

sources.title: CIA Africa Review ALA AR85-022
sources.access: Official indexed primary passage; direct PDF redirected to CIA homepage in this run
sources.finding: Describes ill-trained regular forces, desertion and draft avoidance, equipment-operation difficulties, and dependence on Zimbabwean assistance. Supports a modest late-war readiness reduction rather than a universal extreme rating.

sources.title: CIA Mozambique assessment, RDP85T01058R000100440004-4
sources.finding: Describes leadership, morale and supply problems, and gradual prospective benefits of foreign retraining. Corroborates the 1985 readiness judgement; precise publication day not established here.

sources.title: UN ONUMOZ background: formation of Mozambican defence force
sources.finding: Instructor training in 1993 and infantry training in 1994 accompanied the new army formation. Integration was an ongoing process, not instant improvement in tactical competence.

sources.title: Secretary-General ONUMOZ progress report S/1994/1002
sources.finding: Records incomplete recruitment/training and transfer from the former army in August1994. Supports keeping the new FADM at a restrained baseline rather than automatically raising quality because of the new identity.
